notes: Original embedded images extracted byte-for-byte. DOCX page references use the document list of figures. Existing annotations, crops and masking are preserved. No complete theses are deployed.

documents.clp: Wazuh SIEM Detection Engineering and Noise Reduction (PDF)

additional_figures.title: Endpoints, enrolled and active
additional_figures.caption: Five agents are shown as active, with their groups, operating systems, and versions. The annotations and masked addresses are preserved from the thesis.
additional_figures.alt: Wazuh agent table showing five active Ubuntu endpoints, with source annotations and masked IP addresses.

additional_figures.title: Endpoint events reach the dashboard
additional_figures.caption: The event view shows records from the enrolled agent alongside rule IDs, connecting endpoint collection to analyst review.
additional_figures.alt: Wazuh event histogram and event rows, with the agent name and rule IDs highlighted in the original screenshot.

additional_figures.title: Parse runtime events
additional_figures.caption: A Tetragon base decoder identifies the event source; the child decoder uses JSON_Decoder to parse the record.
additional_figures.alt: Original XML defining tetragon-base and tetragon-json decoders with the JSON_Decoder plugin.

additional_figures.title: Extract indicator fields
additional_figures.caption: The MISP test decoders extract domain and URL fields so that later rules can evaluate the parsed values.
additional_figures.alt: Original MISP decoder XML with domain and url_noscheme prematch, regex, and order fields.

additional_figures.title: Inspect the decoded runtime record
additional_figures.caption: The expanded event exposes the Tetragon decoder, source log, rule 732011, and ATT&CK mapping. It is a recorded lab alert, not live telemetry.
additional_figures.alt: Expanded Wazuh document showing tetragon-base, the tetragon.log source, rule 732011, and a cron-related ATT&CK mapping.

additional_figures.title: Before tuning: repeated routine events
additional_figures.caption: The thesis’s before view contains repeated PAM session and sudo records. It illustrates the noise that motivated rule tuning.
additional_figures.alt: Original before-tuning Wazuh event list with repeated session-open, session-close, and sudo events.

additional_figures.title: After tuning: retained SSH context
additional_figures.caption: The after view retains the successful-login records. These screenshots illustrate the change; their different timestamps do not support a measured reduction percentage.
additional_figures.alt: Original after-tuning Wazuh screenshot showing retained successful SSH login events and highlighted rule 118007.

additional_figures.title: Indicator matches in the alert view
additional_figures.caption: The captured alert rows include MISP URL and domain matches, plus a file-integrity hash match, with their rule IDs and priorities.
additional_figures.alt: Wazuh alert rows for a MISP URL match, a MISP domain match, and a known malicious SHA256 file-hash match.

additional_figures.title: Map the analyst to read-only access
additional_figures.caption: The role mapping connects the lab SOC analyst account to the readonly role. This screenshot records the configuration; access testing is reported separately in the thesis.
additional_figures.alt: Original Wazuh role-mapping form connecting soc_analyst-1 to the readonly role, with numbered source annotations.

additional_figures.title: LAN to DMZ: service exposure
additional_figures.caption: The scan of 172.16.40.10 reports HTTP, HTTPS, and PostgreSQL reachable from the LAN assessment position.
additional_figures.alt: Nmap output for the DMZ host showing ports 80, 443, and 5432 open, highlighted in the original screenshot.

additional_figures.title: LAN to directory services
additional_figures.caption: The directory-server scan records reachable DNS, Kerberos, LDAP, SMB, and related services. Open services establish exposure, not successful exploitation.
additional_figures.alt: Nmap service scan of Active Directory host 172.16.30.10, listing open directory and Windows service ports.

additional_figures.title: LAN to the backup host
additional_figures.caption: The backup-host scan records SSH and an SSL/HTTP service on port 51515, alongside closed and filtered ports.
additional_figures.alt: Nmap scan of 172.16.30.20 showing ports 22 and 51515 open and several other tested ports closed or filtered.

additional_figures.title: Configure the controlled phishing exercise
additional_figures.caption: The GoPhish campaign form connects an email template, landing page, and lab URL. This figure documents campaign setup, not its outcome.
additional_figures.alt: GoPhish campaign configuration for an initial-access simulation, using the lab address 172.16.10.100.

additional_figures.title: Run the discovery profile
additional_figures.caption: CALDERA records successful discovery steps for users, processes, domain information, and security software. This is evidence of those steps, not a complete automated attack chain.
additional_figures.alt: CALDERA operation table showing successful discovery abilities on the win-3 lab host.

additional_figures.title: Inspect privileged group membership
additional_figures.caption: BloodHound visualizes the lab account’s group relationships, making the directory privilege model reviewable.
additional_figures.alt: BloodHound graph and member-of panel showing the lab ROOT account linked to directory groups.

additional_figures.title: Trace relationships to domain control
additional_figures.caption: The graph shows directory groups connected to the domain through GenericAll and AllExtendedRights relationships. The figure records analyzed permissions, not an exploit replay.
additional_figures.alt: BloodHound graph showing Enterprise Admins, Administrators, and Domain Admins linked to the lab domain by permission relationships.

additional_figures.title: Review web scanner findings
additional_figures.caption: ZAP lists potential information-disclosure and configuration findings. Scanner observations require validation before being treated as confirmed vulnerabilities.
additional_figures.alt: ZAP alerts panel listing disclosure, content-security-policy, hidden-file, and header findings for the lab web server.

additional_figures.title: Check certificate identity and trust
additional_figures.caption: The testssl.sh output flags a domain-name mismatch and an incomplete chain of trust. Its displayed rating is explicitly marked experimental.
additional_figures.alt: Original testssl.sh rating output with domain-name mismatch and chain-of-trust grade-cap reasons.
